power_domains_summary.VCC: Main supply 3.3 V (or 1.8 V for low-voltage variants). Powers all TPM logic.
power_domains_summary.VBAT: Optional battery-backed pin for monotonic-clock continuity when host VCC is removed (vendor option).

power_up_sequence: 1. Platform applies VCC to TPM (3.3 V or 1.8 V per chip).
2. Platform deasserts TPM reset (PLTRST# or dedicated reset).
3. TPM runs internal self-test on critical algorithms.
4. TPM enters Init state; commands return TPM_RC_INITIALIZE.
5. Platform firmware issues TPM2_Startup(TPM_SU_CLEAR) — TPM transitions to Operation state.

low_power_modes_summary.Idle: Between commands; TPM_STS.commandReady=1; vendor may gate internal clocks.
low_power_modes_summary.S3_sleep: Platform issues TPM2_Shutdown(TPM_SU_STATE) before host S3 suspend; TPM saves state to NV; VCC may be removed.
low_power_modes_summary.S4_S5: Platform issues TPM2_Shutdown(TPM_SU_CLEAR); TPM does a clean halt.
low_power_modes_summary.Power_off: VCC removed; volatile state lost; non-volatile state preserved in NV (seeds, persistent objects, NV indices, DA counter, clock-safe).
low_power_modes_summary.Field_upgrade: Vendor firmware-update mode; only TPM2_FieldUpgradeData accepted.

rows: Peak up to 80 mA for several seconds (vendor)

fields.monotonic_clock_persistence: The TPM maintains a clock (TPMS_CLOCK_INFO.clock) that accumulates only while the TPM has power. The reset count + restart count are non-volatile. A VBAT-backed implementation can maintain clock across host power loss.
fields.notes: Power scheme is delegated to TIS/PTP. Architecture Part 1 only normatively requires that hierarchies and NV indices retain their state across power-off, and that TPM2_Startup is the first command after each power cycle.

extraction_hints: Look for power-domain partitioning, supply nets.
